title: Present Simple: Positive Statements
description: Express habits, universal truths, and daily repeated actions using affirmative present simple verbs.
objectives: Identify the communicative purposes of the present simple tense (habits, routines, facts)
Form positive statements with pronouns (I, you, we, they + base verb; he, she, it + verb-s)
Interpret the tense timeline illustrating repeated regular actions across past, present, and future

sections.title: Mastering the Present Simple Tense
sections.content:
We use the **Present Simple** tense to speak about things that happen **regularly**, **habitual actions**, or things that are **always true**.

It is not used for what is happening right this second; it describes your permanent life habits and universal realities.

tables.title: Form / Use / Signal Words / Common Mistakes
rows: I work / You study / They live in Lahore
No suffixes added to the verb.
He works / She studies / It rains
Must add -s/-es for singular third person.
The sun rises in the east / I drink coffee
Every day, always, usually, often, on Mondays
I run every morning / She usually wakes early
Incorrect: 'He live here' -> Correct: 'He lives here'

callouts.title: Habit vs. Right Now
callouts.text: Do not use Present Simple for an action happening at this exact second (that is Present Continuous). Say: 'I drink water every day' (habit) vs 'I am drinking water now'.

callouts.title: The SVO Order Rule
callouts.text: English strictly follows Subject + Verb + Object. Say: 'I (S) drink (V) tea (O)', never 'I tea drink'.

timeline.title: Repeated Habit Across Time
timeline.present: I drink tea every morning (Current repeating habit)
timeline.explanation: Present simple indicates regular repeating points over time, not a single momentary action.

sections.title: Lesson Summary
sections.content: Mastery points for Present Simple affirmative:
summaryPoints: Use Present Simple for habits, routines, and universal truths.
I, You, We, They + Base Verb (I work, we study).
He, She, It + Verb-s / -es (He works, she studies).
Follow SVO word order: Subject + Verb + Object (I drink tea).
Signal words include: every day, always, usually, on Mondays.
